paper_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

knowledge_points.content: Four batches of conjugated block copolymers (CBCs) named PB-b-PY-1, PB-b-PY-2, PB-b-PY-3, and PB-b-PY-4 were synthesized via a one-pot polymerization method where the donor block (DB) polymerization time (T1) was varied (0, 80, 160, and 240 minutes, respectively) while keeping the total reaction time at 6 hours.
knowledge_points.evidence: Note that the one-pot polymerization time was controlled at 6 h (T1 + T2 = 6 h), and four batches of PBDB-T-b-PYT copolymers, including PB-b-PY-1 (T1 = 0 min), PB-b-PY-2 (T1 = 80 min), PB-b-PY-3 (T1 = 160 min), and PB-b-PY-4 (T1 = 240 min), were achieved by adjusting the T1 periods.

knowledge_points.content: The single-component organic solar cell (SCOSC) based on PB-b-PY-4 achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.28%, with an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.92 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 21.87 mA cm^-2, and a fill factor (FF) of 66.0%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Among these CBCs, the PB-b-PY-4-based SMOsCs achieved the highest photovoltaic performance with a PCE of 13.28% (Voc = 0.92 V, Jsc = 21.87 mA cm^-2, FF = 66.0%).

knowledge_points.content: Increasing the polymerization time (T1) of the donor block leads to a higher intensity ratio of donor block absorption to acceptor block absorption (ID/IA), indicating that the conjugation length of the PBDB-T block increases with longer T1.
knowledge_points.evidence: As T1 increases, the peaks for DB get sharper and the ratios of intensity for DB and AB (ID/IA) increase gradually... it can be referred that the ID/IA variation in these copolymers originates from different block lengths in these polymers.

knowledge_points.content: Grazing incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) analysis shows that PB-b-PY-4 exhibits a crystal coherence length (CCL) of 96.81 Å for the (100) lamellar stacking peak in the in-plane (IP) direction, which is significantly higher than the 39.767 Å observed for PB-b-PY-2.
knowledge_points.evidence: The (100) peaks in IP direction for PB-b-PY-2, PB-b-PY-3, and PB-b-PY-4 located at 0.31, 0.30, and 0.30 Å^-1... corresponding to... CCL of 39.767, 83.22, and 96.81 Å respectively, demonstrating increasing packing order of lamellar stacking in CBCs with longer DB length.

knowledge_points.content: The charge recombination analysis reveals that the PB-b-PY-4 device has a lower trap-assisted recombination slope of 1.39 kT/q and a higher power-law alpha value of 0.983 for Jsc vs. light intensity, indicating suppressed bimolecular recombination compared to PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3.
knowledge_points.evidence: The slope of the PB-b-PY-4 device was 1.39 kT q^-1 which is much lower than those of the PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3 devices... The alpha values are 0.935 for PB-b-PY-2, 0.961 for PB-b-PY-3, and 0.983 for PB-b-PY-4, respectively, suggesting lower bimolecular recombination loss in the PB-b-PY-4 devices.

knowledge_points.content: Charge carrier mobilities measured by the space charge limited current (SCLC) method for PB-b-PY-4 were balanced, with a hole mobility (μh) of 4.22 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and an electron mobility (μe) of 4.24 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1.
knowledge_points.evidence: all of the single-component films have balanced mobilities with... μh of 4.22 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and μe of 4.24 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 (μh/μe ≈ 1) for PB-b-PY-4.

knowledge_points.content: The PB-b-PY-4 based SCOSC shows superior photostability, retaining 87% of its initial PCE after 340 hours of continuous light-soaking under one-sun illumination, whereas PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3 retained only 63% and 72%, respectively.
knowledge_points.evidence: Impressively, after 340 h light-soaking, 87% of its initial PCE was retained by the PB-b-PY-4-based devices, while it's 72% and 63% for PB-b-PY-3-and PB-b-PY-2-based devices over the same period, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Steady-state photoluminescence (PL) quenching efficiency increases with the conjugation length of the donor block, reaching 85.4% for PB-b-PY-4 compared to 71.6% for PB-b-PY-2, indicating more effective charge transfer in materials with longer donor blocks.
knowledge_points.evidence: the PL quenching efficiencies of PB-b-PY-2, PB-b-PY-3, and PB-b-PY-4 was 71.6%, 80.9%, and 85.4%, respectively. The increasing quenching efficiency indicated that as the DB conjugation length increases, charge transfer from acceptor block to donor block gets more effective.

knowledge_points.content: The exciton dissociation and charge collection probability (Jsc/Jsat) for the PB-b-PY-4 device was calculated to be 94.83%, which is higher than the 63.31% and 86.37% observed for PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3, respectively.
knowledge_points.evidence: The JMPP/Jsat and Jsc/Jsat values were calculated as 30.79%/63.31% for PB-b-PY-2, 57.79%/86.37% for PB-b-PY-3, and 74.44%/94.83% for PB-b-PY-4, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: The SCOSC devices were fabricated using a conventional architecture: ITO/PEDOT:PSS/CBCs/PDINN/Ag, where PDINN serves as the electron transport layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: SCOsCs were fabricated with a conventional architecture of indium tin oxide (ITO)/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS)/CBCs/aliphatic aminefunctionalized perylene-diimide (PDINN)/ Ag.
